items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: Miles Davis was smart when he got with Parker

ctx.x: But Erroll Garner could play faster notes than I could play. He was a taught person. And it was a thing called the up and down stroke, which makes you produce the speed as far as playing, whereas I had mostly a down-- I had a wrist, like Montgomery had his thumb. All downstrokes, but eventually it got it. It takes time you're supposed to learn that from they start. He could do that very good so the fast tunes were no problem. They used to give me a problem. . . .

I was always told that if you learned how to read music, and learn how to play like this you'd be mechanical. That didn't occur to only me -- hundreds of us out here. Which was dumb. Miles Davis was smart when he got with Parker, and he found that he couldn't really cut that stuff too good, but he took himself off to Juilliard and stayed down there and got it together, and come back. He's one of the greatest in the world. That's using your brain. But we'd say "no man, I don't want to be mechanical" so we don't…
How did you first meet Parker? Was it after you the Tatum trio broke up?
